COMM_W4_Partner_with_a_Local_Group_or_Ch.title: Partnership authenticity audit
COMM_W4_Partner_with_a_Local_Group_or_Ch.purpose: Build professional partnership reasoning while enforcing contact and data boundaries.

activity.prompt: Predict which partnership check will most change the project. Select the complete set for an authentic, authorised partnership.

statements.label: The organisation and contact route are verified through an official or centre-approved source.
statements.reason: The group knows who it is approaching.

statements.label: The project team identifies a specific reason the partnership could be useful to both sides.
statements.reason: Contact has purpose and reciprocity.

statements.label: Pupils message personal accounts directly because it is quicker.
statements.reason: External contact follows the authorised adult route.

statements.label: The partner’s real priorities, capacity and boundaries are heard and recorded accurately.
statements.reason: Partnership changes the plan rather than rubber-stamping it.

statements.label: The team promises outcomes before the partner has agreed.
statements.reason: Commitments cannot be invented.

statements.label: Consent, safeguarding, data, travel and recording requirements are checked.
statements.reason: Participation remains within centre processes.

statements.label: A real response is stored or referenced through the authorised evidence route.
statements.reason: The partnership is authentic and traceable.

statements.label: No reply is replaced with a fictional acceptance so planning can continue.
statements.reason: No response remains no response.

activity.completion: A partnership is verified, purposeful, reciprocal, authorised and capable of changing the plan; contact alone is not partnership evidence.
predictionOptions: Verification will change the plan most
The partner’s capacity will change it most
Safeguarding/data requirements will change it most

COMM_W6_Promote_Our_Project.title: Promotion truth-and-access audit
COMM_W6_Promote_Our_Project.purpose: Move promotion from visual decoration to audience-centred, evidence-led communication.

activity.prompt: Predict which communication check will most affect trust. Select everything a safe, truthful promotion needs.

statements.label: A clear purpose and intended audience.
statements.reason: The format and message can be judged against a real need.

statements.label: Accurate project facts and a proportionate claim about current progress.
statements.reason: Promotion does not outrun evidence.

statements.label: Names, faces or stories of participants used without filed permission.
statements.reason: Consent and data boundaries apply.

statements.label: An accessible route such as readable layout, captions or an equivalent format.
statements.reason: Audience access is planned.

statements.label: A specific call to action that the audience can actually complete.
statements.reason: The message leads to a defined next step.

statements.label: An invented impact statistic to make the project sound important.
statements.reason: Only real, contextualised evidence can support impact.

statements.label: Partner name or logo used only with the agreed permission and wording.
statements.reason: Representation is authorised.

statements.label: A publication and responsible-adult check through the centre’s route.
statements.reason: Pupil drafting does not itself authorise release.

activity.completion: Trustworthy promotion is accurate, accessible, consented and proportionate, with a real call to action and authorised publication route.
predictionOptions: Claim accuracy will matter most
Consent will matter most
Accessibility will matter most
